---

## Financial Accounting (FI)

SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting centers on the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), which merges general ledger, controlling, asset, and material-ledger line items into one multi-dimensional single source of truth, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation. Around that core sit Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, automatic payment runs), Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, dunning, incoming payments), Asset Accounting (ledger-based parallel valuation and depreciation), Bank and Cash Management, tax determination via tax codes and procedures, real-time financial statements drawn directly from the journal, and orchestrated period-end/year-end close. Distinctive S/4HANA traits practitioners flag as essential include parallel ledgers for multi-GAAP accounting, document splitting for dimension-complete balance sheets, up to 10 parallel currencies, and posting-period control.

| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General Ledger on the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)** | Full | finance | — |
| **Chart of accounts and fiscal year / posting period control** | Full | finance | — |
| **Multi-currency accounting and foreign currency valuation** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 (PLAN 4.3 done) has transaction + functional currency, a rates table (SPOT/CLOSING, direct-or-inverse lookup), posting-time translation with frozen functional amounts (largest-remainder residual balancing), purpose-keyed FX posting defaults, and an **unrealized**-FX revaluation run with auto-reversal. **Bounded out of v1:** group/additional parallel currencies; consolidation-style translation; **realized** FX (deferred to AP/AR clearing — purposes wired now); and **per-open-item** revaluation granularity — v1 revalues the per-account monetary foreign balance (accounts flagged `is_monetary` with a foreign `currency_code`), not individual uncleared AP/AR items. Later: add per-line extra currency columns + open-item-granular revaluation + realized FX at clearing, reusing the same rates-table and FX-account machinery. |
| **Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, payment runs, aging)** | Full | finance | Core AP (vendor bills, payment runs, aging) is planned; bank payment file formats (ISO 20022/NACHA) and withholding tax are not explicitly in v1. Later: Layer payment-media file generation and withholding tax codes onto the existing payment-run engine. |
| **Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, receipts, dunning, aging)** | Full | finance | — |
| **Asset Accounting (parallel valuation, full lifecycle)** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 is "asset accounting lite": register plus straight-line and declining-balance depreciation runs posting journals; no parallel depreciation areas, transfers, retirements with gain/loss, revaluation, or assets under construction. Later: Extend the asset register with lifecycle events (transfer/retire/AuC settle) and per-ledger depreciation areas reusing the existing depreciation-run poster. |
| **Bank and Cash Management** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 covers bank reconciliation via CSV statement import with match suggestions only; no standard bank formats (MT940/CAMT), no auto-clearing rules engine, no cash positioning or liquidity forecasting. Later: Add MT940/CAMT.053 parsers feeding the same import pipeline, then a cash-position report over bank-clearing accounts. |
| **Tax handling (tax codes, determination, compliance reporting)** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 plans line-level configurable tax codes (rate, jurisdiction, inclusive/exclusive) — the calculation core — but no withholding tax, no statutory tax return reports, and no external tax engine integration. Later: Build tax-return reports as queries over tax-coded journal lines and add a pluggable external tax-calculation interface. |
| **Financial statements and real-time reporting** | Full | finance | — |
| **Period-end and year-end close** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 has the enforcement primitives (period open/close at service and DB level, FX revaluation accounts, depreciation runs) but no year-end balance carryforward, accrual engine, GR/IR regrouping, or close task orchestration. Later: Add a balance-carryforward job and a simple checklist-style close task list on top of existing period states. |
| **Parallel ledgers and document splitting (multi-GAAP)** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 plans a single universal-journal ledger; no parallel/extension ledgers or document splitting — the boundary is single-GAAP, entity-level balance sheets only (dimensions exist on lines but are not balanced). Later: Introduce a ledger dimension on journal entries so postings can fan out to parallel ledgers, then add a splitting rule engine at posting time. |
| Credit, collections and dispute management (Receivables Management/FSCM) | Out of scope | — | Not in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 AR stops at invoices, receipts, dunning levels, and aging — credit/collections/disputes are S/4HANA add-on processes beyond core FI-AR. Later: Add credit limits on the customer master with a posting-time check, then collections worklists driven by the existing aging data. |

---

## Controlling (CO)

In current S/4HANA, Controlling is no longer a separate ledger world: FI and CO are merged into the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), so every posting carries cost center, profit center, project/WBS, order, and profitability-segment dimensions, and all CO reporting is a real-time projection of that single table; cost elements have become G/L accounts. The practitioner-essential core comprises cost center accounting, profit center accounting, internal orders (deprecated in S/4HANA Cloud in favor of project cost collectors), product cost planning and cost object controlling, Margin Analysis (account-based CO-PA), universal allocations, activity types with internal activity allocation, and cost center planning/budgeting, with Material Ledger actual costing as an optional deepening. Atlas v1's design matches the architectural core and S/4HANA Cloud's direction (including replacing internal orders with projects), but leaves activity-rate machinery, planning/budgeting, variance decomposition, and multi-dimensional margin segments for later.

| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Universal Journal merge of FI and CO** | Full | finance | — |
| **Cost center accounting (CO-OM-CCA)** | Full | finance | — |
| **Profit center accounting** | Full | finance | — |
| **Internal orders (CO-OM-OPA)** | Partial | projects | Atlas deliberately mirrors S/4HANA Cloud's "Principle of One" by covering the cost-collector role with projects/WBS instead of a separate order object, but order-specific machinery (order types, statistical orders, settlement rules to cost centers/assets, budget availability control) is not stated in the plan. Later: Extend projects with settlement rules, budget/availability control, and settlement-to-asset postings rather than introducing a separate order object. |
| **Product cost planning (standard cost estimates)** | Partial | manufacturing | Atlas plans manufacturing-fed product costing (actual costs, WIP, finish-to-stock valuation) but does not state a BOM/routing cost-rollup engine, cost component split, or standard price release/costing-run machinery. Later: Add a cost-rollup service over BOM/routing data that produces standard costs with a component split, used to value finished-goods receipts and compute variances. |
| **Cost object controlling (WIP, variances, settlement)** | Partial | manufacturing | Atlas plans the core flow — WIP journals and finish-to-stock postings, which matches S/4HANA's modern event-based direction — but variance decomposition (input price/quantity, resource usage, lot size), scrap analysis, and settlement profiles are not planned. Later: Add variance categorization computed from journal deltas at order close, posting categorized variance lines to the ledger and the margin report. |
| **Margin analysis / profitability analysis (CO-PA)** | Partial | reporting | Atlas plans a margin-by-product report projected from the ledger — the right account-based architecture — but only the product dimension; customer/region/channel segments, COGS split by cost component, top-down distribution, and realignments are not planned. Later: Widen journal lines with additional market-segment attributes (customer, region, channel) derived at posting time and add segment-level margin reports over the same ledger projection. |
| **Allocations and assessments (universal allocation)** | Full | finance | Atlas plans allocation rules on cost centers and profit centers posting through the journal, which is the practitioner-essential core; allocation to margin-analysis segments and plan-data allocation are the main S/4 extras not mentioned. Later: Add margin-segment-context and plan-data allocation cycles on the same rule engine. |
| **Activity types and internal activity allocation** | Out of scope | — | No activity-type master, rate planning/calculation, or rate-based secondary cost postings appear in the Atlas plan; production cost capture is implied to be direct journal entries without rate machinery, so conversion-cost absorption from cost centers has no planned mechanism. Later: Add activity types with planned rates that generate secondary-cost journal lines from production confirmations, crediting the supplying cost center and debiting the order. |
| **Cost planning and budgeting (plan/actual)** | Out of scope | — | The Atlas v1 plan covers only actuals; no plan ledger, budget entry, or plan/actual comparison is mentioned, yet plan-versus-actual on cost centers is a core controlling activity for practitioners. Later: Add a plan-line ledger parallel to the journal and extend the cost-center and margin reports with plan/actual/variance columns. |
| Material Ledger / actual costing | Out of scope | — | Not mentioned in the Atlas plan; actual costing is an optional deepening in S/4HANA (mandatory only as the multi-currency valuation substructure), so omitting it from v1 is a defensible cut. Later: Add a periodic actual-cost roll-up job that recomputes inventory and COGS values from accumulated journal lines and posts revaluation entries. |

# CLAUDE.md — Permanent Project Memory for Atlas ERP

Atlas ERP is an open-source, industry-agnostic ERP platform. Its explicit functional benchmark is **SAP S/4HANA**. Everything in this file is binding for every working session.

## Session protocol (read this first, always)

1. **After any compaction or new session: read CLAUDE.md, PLAN.md, PROGRESS.md, and DECISIONS.md before writing any code.** Verify the last PROGRESS.md entry against the actual code and `git log`, then resume from the next unchecked PLAN.md task. Never guess at prior state.
2. **All file creation, naming, and placement MUST follow STRUCTURE.md. Re-read it after any compaction.** Before creating any new file, run `git status` and inspect the tree to re-anchor on actual structure.
3. **All git and GitHub operations MUST follow GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md. Re-read it after any compaction.** Branch model: `main` (production, promotion PRs only) ← `dev` (integration) ← short-lived feature branches. Issue-first for every discovered problem.
4. **All code MUST comply with PERFORMANCE.md. Re-read it after any compaction.** Every endpoint's Definition of Done includes the PERFORMANCE.md §6 checklist: FK + filter columns indexed, query-count assertion passes (≤3 per list request), paginated, money is Decimal, heavy work bulk/background, perf-suite coverage for hot paths. Target: 50 concurrent users on a 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS within the §5 latency budgets.
5. Work in small units: implement one task → run its tests → commit → update PROGRESS.md → next task. **Definition of done: code written, tests passing, committed, logged in PROGRESS.md** — plus, for endpoints, the PERFORMANCE.md §6 checklist. A task that isn't committed and logged does not exist.
6. Append one line to PROGRESS.md after every completed task and tick the checkbox in PLAN.md. Record every consequential design decision in DECISIONS.md the moment it is made.
7. No pseudocode, no placeholders, no stubs, no TODO comments. Every file must be complete and working. When scope forces a trade-off, choose a smaller surface that fully works, and record the cut in `docs/research/s4hana-parity.md`.

## Tech stack (non-negotiable)

- **Backend:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (typed, async), PostgreSQL-first models (SQLite-compatible for the demo/test run), Alembic migrations, Pydantic v2. Dependency manager: **uv** (`uv.lock` committed).
- **Frontend:** React 18 + TypeScript + Vite, TanStack Query + TanStack Router, Tailwind. In-house component library only (data grid, form builder, kanban, dashboard cards, document-flow viewer). Fiori-inspired role-based home pages. Package manager: npm.
- **API:** REST, versioned `/api/v1`, OpenAPI docs, cursor pagination, consistent error envelope, idempotency keys on every endpoint that creates a financial or stock document.

## Architecture rules (hardcoded inheritances from S/4HANA)

1. **Universal Journal:** one append-only financial line-item table is the single source of truth. All FI and CO views (P&L, balance sheet, cost-center reports, margin analysis) are projections of it — never separately stored totals.
2. **Document flow:** every business document (PO, receipt, delivery, invoice, journal…) records its predecessor/successor links; the UI can render the full chain for any document.
3. **Multi-tenancy:** row-level `tenant_id` on every table, enforced by a session-level filter that query authors cannot bypass.
4. **Auth & RBAC:** JWT access+refresh, argon2 hashing; roles → permissions → resources as data (`finance.journal.post`); field-level read masking for HR compensation/IDs.
5. **Audit:** append-only audit table (actor, tenant, entity, before/after diff, timestamp, IP) written by middleware, not per-endpoint code.
6. **Event bus:** in-process domain-event dispatcher decouples modules (`SalesOrderShipped` → inventory issues stock → finance posts COGS); swappable for Kafka/Redis without touching business logic. Cross-module effects go through events; synchronous cross-module reads only via the owning module's `queries.py` (see STRUCTURE.md §5).
7. **Service layer owns business rules; routers thin; models logic-free.** Financial invariants live in code AND DB constraints (e.g. CHECK: exactly one of debit/credit > 0 per line).
8. Posted journal entries are immutable; corrections only via reversing entries. Postings to closed periods are rejected at service AND DB level.

## Coding conventions

Naming, file placement, size caps (400-line Python / 300-line TSX), import rules, and the terminology lock are defined in STRUCTURE.md §7–§8. Canonical terms: `item` (not product/sku), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override display labels, never internal names.

## Build order (strict — from PLAN.md)

0. State files → 1. S/4HANA research + parity doc → 2. Full plan + key decisions → 3. `core/` (tenancy, auth, RBAC, audit, events, docflow, numbering, base models) → 4. Finance/Controlling → 5. Inventory → 6. Procurement → 7. Sales → 8. Manufacturing → 9. Quality/Maintenance → 10. HR → 11. Projects → 12. CRM → 13. Reporting → 14. Admin + onboarding → 15. Frontend design system, then module UIs in the same order → 16. Seed data → 17. README/diagrams/parity reconciliation.

Tests and commits accompany every step, never batched at the end. If scope must be cut: cut frontend polish before backend correctness, and module breadth before financial-engine depth — and record every cut in the parity doc.

## Environment notes (this machine)

- `uv` and `python3.12` live at `~/.local/bin/` (not on default PATH in fresh shells; invoke as `~/.local/bin/uv`).
- Backend commands run from `backend/`: `uv sync`, `uv run pytest -q`, `uv run ruff check .`
- Frontend commands run from `frontend/`: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`.
- GitHub repo: `Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp` (public). CI = `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, jobs `backend` + `frontend`; both are required status checks on `main` and `dev`.

# DECISIONS.md — Design Decision Log

One line per consequential decision + rationale, so later sessions don't re-litigate or contradict earlier choices. Numbered, append-only; superseding a decision gets a new entry referencing the old one.

- **D-001 Bootstrap exception to "nothing directly on main":** the `.gitignore` root commit lands directly on `main` (GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §1 explicitly orders it first); everything else reaches `main` only via `dev` promotions. Rationale: a branch cannot be cut from an empty repo.
- **D-002 Python toolchain = uv + Python 3.12:** uv manages the venv, lockfile (`uv.lock`, committed) and Python pin; CI uses `astral-sh/setup-uv`. Rationale: fastest reproducible installs, single tool for venv+lock+run.
- **D-003 Tests on SQLite (aiosqlite), runtime on PostgreSQL:** models are written PostgreSQL-first with SQLite-compatible type fallbacks (e.g. JSON variant for JSONB, Numeric for money); the full suite and CI run against in-memory/file SQLite, while docker-compose runs Postgres. Rationale: the prompt requires PostgreSQL-first + SQLite-compatible demo; SQLite keeps CI fast and dependency-free. DB-level financial constraints must be expressed portably (CHECK constraints, not Postgres-only features) or get Postgres-only guards documented per case.
- **D-004 Frontend package manager = npm:** lockfile committed; no pnpm/yarn. Rationale: zero extra tooling on contributor machines.
- **D-005 CI check names are stable from PR #1:** single workflow `ci.yml` with jobs `backend` and `frontend`; each job no-ops green while its directory doesn't exist yet. Rationale: branch protection requires named status checks; names must exist before the code does.
- **D-006 Makefile and docker-compose.yml are deferred to the first backend PR:** a Makefile whose targets point at directories that don't exist would violate the no-orphan-files rule in spirit. Rationale: every committed file must work the day it lands.
- **D-007 Tenancy via non-bypassable session filter:** a `do_orm_execute` hook adds `with_loader_criteria(TenantMixin, ...)` reading a `current_tenant_id` ContextVar to every ORM statement (lazy loads and bulk writes included), fail-closed when unset unless `system_context()` is active (exactly four call sites); `before_flush` stamps/validates tenant_id; composite `(tenant_id, id)` FKs + SQLite `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` are the DB backstop. Only mechanism with zero cooperation from query authors. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-008 JWT access+refresh with CAS rotation and 10 s grace window:** HS256 with `ATLAS_JWT_SECRET`; 15-min stateless access token with `ver` checked against `core_users.token_version`; 14-day refresh JWT in an httpOnly cookie scoped to /api/v1/auth, rotated via compare-and-swap on hashed jti in `core_refresh_sessions` with reuse → family revocation, prev-jti accepted within 10 s so multi-tab races don't force logouts; argon2id (t=3, m=65536, p=4) off-thread. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-009 RBAC as data + partial-bound WrapSerializer masking:** code-defined `core_permissions` catalog, tenant-scoped `core_roles` + join tables; `require_permission(key)` dependency resolves effective permissions in one join query, TTL-cached 60 s keyed on (tenant, user, token_version); field masking via `Masked(tp, permission)` WrapSerializer reading a `current_permissions` ContextVar, masked fields excluded from Update schemas. Tenants can't invent keys no code checks. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-010 Split-phase audit capture in-transaction:** `before_flush` diffs updates/deletes from attribute history, `after_flush` captures inserts (generated PKs), `after_flush_postexec` writes one Core insert to append-only `core_audit_log` in the same transaction; per-dialect triggers (ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY) forbid update/delete; ORM bulk writes on audited models are hard errors. Audit is exactly as atomic as the change. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-011 In-process event bus, collect-then-dispatch in-transaction:** `publish()` buffers in session.info; `run_in_uow()` drains FIFO before commit, handlers share the session (cap 50, cycle error), any handler failure rolls back everything — goods issue without COGS can never commit. `events.py` becomes a sanctioned declarative cross-module import (STRUCTURE §5 amendment); swap path is an outbox bus behind the same Protocol. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-012 Document registry + flow links + gapless numbering (merged):** `core_documents` registry (nullable doc_no, partial unique index) with `DocumentMixin` NOT NULL document_id, `core_doc_links` edges traversed by one recursive CTE; numbers from `core_number_sequences` via atomic UPDATE...RETURNING, claimed only in the transaction that makes a document permanent (drafts numbered at posting) — so gaplessness falls out of ACID with no burned numbers. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-013 Idempotency by PK reservation + atomic route capture:** `core_idempotency_keys` PK(tenant, endpoint, key); guard inserts 'in_progress' in a separate committed transaction (concurrent duplicates collide), replays stored responses on completed+matching hash; the handler's `idem.capture(schema)` stages the completed UPDATE on the business session so replay record and document commit atomically — fail-closed if capture is forgotten. Required on every financial/stock-document endpoint. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-014 Keyset pagination + one error envelope + ATLAS_ token translation:** `{items, next_cursor, limit}` with base64url cursors fingerprinting sort+filters, expanded portable seek predicate, never OFFSET; all errors as `{error: {code, message, details, request_id}}` with dot-namespaced codes; a DBAPIError translator maps trigger tokens (ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED etc.) to envelope codes so DB backstops surface like service checks. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-015 Exact money via TypeDecorators (supersedes D-003's "plain Numeric"):** MoneyType/QuantityType (PG NUMERIC(18,6), SQLite INTEGER micro-units ×10^6) and RateType (20,10 / ×10^10); Decimal-only in Python, strings in JSON; quantize ROUND_HALF_UP to currency decimals at posting; single largest-remainder `allocate()` in new `core/money.py` (STRUCTURE §2 amendment); triggers do comparisons and SUMs only. Plain Numeric float-round-trips on SQLite and breaks exact trigger sums. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-016 Custom fields owned by core, not industry:** `core_custom_field_defs` registry + `validate_custom_fields()` + JSONB/JSON `custom_fields` column helper live in new `core/custom_fields.py` (STRUCTURE §2 amendment) — industry-module ownership would force upward imports from finance/inventory; templates and admin CRUD write defs through core services; flat scalar keys only, DECIMAL as strings, portable `.as_string()`-style JSON paths. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-017 Universal journal: one-side CHECK, two-flush posting, reversal-only:** `fin_journal_entries` (nullable entry_number claimed at posting) + `fin_journal_lines` with all CO dimensions, transaction+functional amount pairs, `ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side`; balance trigger on DRAFT→POSTED (ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY), immutability triggers (ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE) allowing only the reversal status mutation; posting mutates loaded lines then header across two flushes; residual functional cent absorbed largest-remainder (no rounding line). Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-018 Period close enforced by per-dialect triggers + service check:** `fin_fiscal_periods`; `trg_fin_entries_period_open` re-derives the period from posting_date on DRAFT→POSTED (plus an INSERT twin) and aborts ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED when no OPEN period covers the date — catching wrong-period-id service bugs; service raises 422 'finance.period_closed' first; close refuses while drafts exist in the period. Triggers are the only cross-table guard on both engines. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-019 FX: posting-time translation, realized at clearing, auto-reversing revaluation:** `fin_exchange_rates` (SPOT/CLOSING), `get_rate()` fails loud on missing rates; functional amounts frozen at posting (largest-remainder balancing); realized gain/loss posted inside the clearing entry via purpose-keyed `fin_posting_defaults`; `run_fx_revaluation` posts one FX_REVAL entry per (currency, account) and its next-period auto-reversal, validating up front that the next period is open. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-020 Inventory costing: moving average + FIFO, same-transaction COGS, no negative stock:** `inv_item_valuations` updated under `with_for_update` (SQLite no-ops it; single-writer lock suffices, pg-marked tests prove the PG path); FIFO via `inv_cost_layers` + `inv_layer_consumptions` with exact reversal replay; the event bus posts the COGS journal entry in the SAME transaction as the move — stock and GL can never diverge; negative stock forbidden by service + CHECKs. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-021 Statements are pure projections of `fin_journal_lines`:** five account types + cash_flow_category on `fin_accounts`; trial balance/P&L/balance sheet/indirect cash flow all derive from ONE aggregate over lines (denormalized is_posted/posting_date, no header join); retained earnings computed cumulatively on the fly; no stored totals anywhere; partial covering index `ix_fin_journal_lines_proj` keeps it sub-second to ~10M lines. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-022 Single Alembic chain on both engines; migrations are the only schema source:** `create_all` banned even in tests (triggers live only in migrations); batch_alter_table everywhere + MetaData naming_convention; per-dialect trigger DDL side by side, re-executed after any batch-alter of a trigger-bearing table (SQLite copy-rebuild silently drops triggers); CI runs full suite on SQLite plus downgrade/upgrade and `-m pg` DB-guard subset on postgres:16. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-023 Hand-written frontend types with a compile-time drift gate:** per-module `types.ts` mirrors Pydantic schemas (Decimal/date/UUID → string, enums → literal unions, Masked → `T | null`); committed `backend/openapi.json` (freshness pytest-asserted) feeds a gitignored openapi-typescript output checked by per-module `types.contract.ts` Equal-assertions in `npm run typecheck` — drift fails CI in both directions with zero runtime cost. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-024 Frontend auth: memory-only access token + boot refresh + cross-tab single-flight:** access token never persisted; httpOnly refresh cookie drives a boot-time silent refresh; proactive renewal at exp−60 s, reactive single-flight retry on 401; `navigator.locks` + BroadcastChannel ensure exactly one tab rotates and the rest adopt the token — eliminating the multi-tab races the backend grace window only softens. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-025 Tests on per-test template copies, not SAVEPOINTs:** a session-scoped fixture migrates ONE template DB (alembic upgrade head); each test gets a file copy (or PG `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE`) so real commits — idempotency reservations, run_in_uow, numbering — work as in production and triggers exist; factories provision through real services; raw-SQL DB-guard tests pin the ATLAS_ tokens on both engines; tenancy suite auto-covers new mappers. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-026 Seed drives the real service layer, deterministically:** `seed.py` provisions five demo tenants from industry templates under system_context, then generates 3 months of interlinked P2P/O2C/production/FX flows through real services in `run_in_uow()` (RNG seeded per template+anchor); months 1-2 closed via the real close service; self-verifies trial balance, docflow chains, and inventory-GL reconciliation; `--reset` is the only sanctioned hard-delete, guarded by the `demo-` slug prefix. Seed doubles as a CI integration smoke gate. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
- **D-027 Core platform tables and the auth router live in `core/`:** `User` (`core_users`) and `RefreshSession` (`core_refresh_sessions`) are defined in `core/models.py` and the login/refresh/logout/me endpoints in a new `core/security_router.py` (prefix `/api/v1/auth`). Rationale: auth/identity are cross-cutting platform concerns belonging to no business module (STRUCTURE §2 litmus — not a business concept), so they stay in `core/` rather than inventing a `modules/auth` package the module list doesn't sanction. `core/auth.py` stays ORM-free (crypto + JWT primitives only). Implements D-008. **Follow-on (PLAN 3.7, same precedent):** the document-flow read endpoint lives in a new `core/docflow_router.py` (`GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/chain`, guarded by `get_current_user`, tenant-scoped) — the document registry is platform infrastructure owned by no module, so its router joins `security_router.py` as a sanctioned core router wired in `create_app()`. Deviations from D-012's draft, all behaviour-preserving: route path is `/api/v1/documents/{id}/chain` (the binding PLAN-task path) not the draft's `/api/v1/core/documents/{id}/flow`; the D-012 numbering/docflow ORM models (`NumberSequence`, `Document`, `DocumentLink`) live in their concern files `core/numbering.py` / `core/docflow.py` (re-exported at the tail of `core/models.py` so they register on `Base.metadata`) rather than in `models.py`, to keep `models.py` under the ~350-line cap — STRUCTURE §2 lists both concern files and §8.5 ("filename promises content") favours co-locating each model with its claim/traversal logic. `core_number_sequences` keys on `(tenant_id, name)` with a `year_reset`/`current_year` pair (the binding task's column spec) rather than the draft's `(tenant_id, doc_type, year)` PK; semantics (gapless in-transaction claim, partial unique index, both-direction recursive CTE) are identical. `claim_number` uses the atomic `UPDATE ... RETURNING` path — verified working on the project's aiosqlite (3.53, >= 3.35), so the sanctioned SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback is unused; `WITH RECURSIVE` likewise verified on aiosqlite.
- **D-028 Idempotency + keyset pagination placement and behaviour (PLAN 3.8, implements D-013/D-014):** the `core_idempotency_keys` model + `reserve`/`IdempotencyContext`/`Idempotent` guard live in a new `core/idempotency.py`; the table uses the NATURAL composite PK `(tenant_id, endpoint, key)` exactly per D-013 (tenant_id overrides TenantMixin to join the PK, keeps `index=True` so the D-007 mapper-enumeration invariant holds). Migration `0007_idempotency`. Deviations, all behaviour-preserving except where noted: (1) the model is registered on `Base.metadata` from the BOTTOM of `core/db.py` (not the `core/models.py` trailing import that numbering/docflow use) because `core/idempotency` imports `core/db` for its session dependencies and `core/db` imports `core/audit`→`core/models`, so a trailing import in models would dead-lock the cycle. (2) The `Idempotent` guard reads `tenant_id` from the D-007 `current_tenant_id` ContextVar (set by `get_current_user`, which guarded routes declare first) rather than importing `CurrentUserDep`, to avoid the `deps`→`db`→`idempotency` import cycle. (3) `capture()` is called INSIDE the `run_in_uow` work so the completion UPDATE and the business document commit in one transaction (Atlas commits via `run_in_uow` inside the handler, not a deferred session-dependency commit). Consequent fail-closed deviation: on a business EXCEPTION the guard's teardown deletes the dangling IN_PROGRESS reservation and re-raises (handlers render the envelope) — fully fail-closed; on a FORGOTTEN `capture()` (handler returned 2xx) the teardown deletes the reservation and logs a server error but cannot convert the already-sent 2xx to a 500, because the `run_in_uow` commit precedes teardown — a documented relaxation of D-013's literal "teardown rolls back" (which assumed a deferred commit). Replay short-circuit: `reserve` raises `IdempotencyReplay` (an AtlasError subtype) whose handler in `app.main` re-emits the stored status+body with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, so a completed-key replay never runs the handler body. **Keyset pagination** lives in a NEW flat core file `core/pagination.py` (`paginate`, `OrderKey`/`SortDirection`, base64url cursor codec with sort+filter fingerprint, `CursorParams`/`cursor_params` with limit cap default 50 / max 200) — STRUCTURE §2 amendment, same precedent as `core/money.py`/`core/custom_fields.py`; this DEVIATES from D-014's letter (which puts `paginate` in `core/db.py` and the codec in `core/schemas.py`) because the keyset machinery is substantial and cross-cutting (§8.5 one-concept-per-file). The `Page` envelope stays in `core/schemas.py`. The seek predicate is written in the EXPANDED portable OR-form unconditionally (verified: this project's aiosqlite 3.53 DOES support uniform-direction row-value tuples, but not MIXED-direction, and Atlas lists mix ASC/DESC, so the expansion is the only universally-correct form on both engines per D-014). Full spec: docs/architecture.md D-013/D-014.
- **D-029 AP/AR sub-ledger is keyed by an opaque `partner_id`, not a finance-owned partner master:** finance is the bottom dependency (everyone may read `finance/queries`; finance imports no module), but the vendor master lives in procurement (PLAN 6) and the customer master in sales (PLAN 7) — both *above* finance. So finance AP/AR open items, payments, dunning and aging are keyed by an opaque `partner_id: UUID` plus a denormalized `partner_name` carried on each document; finance never FK-references a partner table. The vendor/customer masters own the identity (their PK *is* the partner_id) and call finance services to create bills/invoices and run payments. This honors the parity doc's "separate vendor and customer masters, no unified Business Partner" while keeping the dependency direction legal. Realized FX is computed at clearing here (D-019). Trade-off vs a finance-owned `BusinessPartner`: no referential FK from open items to the master (the owning module guarantees the id), accepted for the clean layering.
- **D-031 AR (PLAN 4.6) placement + shared realized-FX clearing helper + dunning (implements D-029/D-019/D-030):** the four AR tables live in `finance/models/receivables.py` (re-exported from `models/__init__`); AR schemas in a NEW sibling `finance/receivables_schemas.py` and the AR endpoints in a NEW sibling `finance/ar_router.py`, both mirroring the sanctioned AP siblings (D-030) and mounting into the finance router via `include_router` (one surface at `/api/v1/finance`). AR is the AP shape with the **sign flipped** (Dr AR control gross / Cr revenue net / Cr output tax at invoice posting; receipts Cr AR / Dr bank) PLUS **dunning**. Service split: `service/customer_invoices.py` (draft+post), `service/customer_receipts.py` (receipt document + clearing), `service/ar_aging.py` (projection), `service/dunning.py`. **Generalized AP's clearing into a shared helper:** AP's `service/payment_clearing.py` was NOT reusable as-is (it took `VendorBill` objects + AP error codes), but the realized-FX MATH is identical at the customer side — so the engine-agnostic core (compute functional amounts, build the balanced clearing journal lines with explicit functional amounts via `skip_translation`, the realized-FX gain/loss line) was factored into a NEW `service/clearing_fx.py` keyed on plain `ClearedItem` tuples + a `control_is_debit` flag (AP debits the control to clear, AR credits it — the gain/loss direction inverts: AP realized = func_control − func_bank, AR realized = func_bank − func_control). `payment_clearing.py` was refactored to adapt bills into `ClearedItem`s and delegate; AR's receipts do the same with invoices — ONE FX implementation, no duplication. **Dunning** (the AR-only escalation, no AP mirror): `DUNNING_THRESHOLDS = (7, 30, 60)` days map to levels 1/2/3 via `dunning_level_for(days_overdue)`; `run_dunning(as_of)` scans OPEN overdue invoices, and when the level their age earns EXCEEDS the invoice's current `dunning_level` it raises it + stamps `last_dunned_date = as_of`, returning the notice list — it posts NO journal (dunning is state only, D-029) and is idempotent-ish per day (a re-run advances nothing already at its earned level). Permissions `finance.ar.read`/`.manage`/`.collect` (collect = receipts + dunning). `queries.py` adds `get_open_customer_invoices` + `customer_open_balance` (the latter for Sales' future credit-limit block, partner-keyed by the opaque `partner_id`). Migration `0013_finance_ar` creates four tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); autogenerate confirms zero drift on SQLite AND Postgres. **Deviation (PG identifier cap):** the D-022 auto FK names for the two `fin_customer_receipt_allocations` composite FKs would be 67 chars (> PG's 63), so the model + migration share explicit abbreviated names (`fk_fin_cust_receipt_allocs_tenant_id_{receipts,invoices}`) — same precedent as AP's abbreviated allocation UNIQUE name (D-030). Finance stays the bottom dependency (imports no module above it; verified); `partner_id` stays opaque (plain Uuid, no FK).
- **D-030 AP (PLAN 4.5) placement + the journal `skip_translation` clearing hook (implements D-029/D-019):** the four AP tables live in `finance/models/payables.py` (re-exported from `models/__init__`); AP request/response schemas live in a NEW sibling `finance/payables_schemas.py` and the AP endpoints in a NEW sibling `finance/ap_router.py` — both siblings (not a `schemas/`/`router/` package) exactly mirror the sanctioned `fx_router.py`/`tax_router.py` precedent, because `schemas.py`/`router.py` are at the STRUCTURE §3 400-line cap and the AP surface is self-contained; `ap_router` mounts into the finance router via the same `include_router` one-surface pattern (no second mount in main.py). The AP service is split across `service/vendor_bills.py` (draft + post), `service/payment_clearing.py` (open-item validation + realized-FX line construction), `service/vendor_payments.py` (payment document + run), and `service/ap_aging.py` (the projection) to keep every file under the cap. **Realized FX at clearing (D-019):** computed per cleared bill as `functional-at-bill-rate − functional-at-payment-rate` over the cleared transaction amount (the bill's frozen rate is read from its posted AP-control journal line, not re-looked-up), posted to the `fx_realized_gain`/`fx_realized_loss` posting-default account inside the SAME payment entry. This required a behaviour-preserving extension to `service/journal.post_entry`: a new keyword `skip_translation: bool = False` — when the caller has already set explicit per-line functional amounts (the only case where functional ≠ transaction × a single entry rate), the engine validates those balance instead of re-translating. The realized-FX line is denominated in the functional currency and carries a positive transaction amount equal to its functional amount, so the per-line one-side CHECK (D-017, on transaction amounts) holds while the balance trigger (functional sums only) balances — no zero/zero line. Open items are partner-keyed by the opaque `partner_id` stamped on the AP control line (D-029); finance imports no module above it (verified). AP documents register in `core_documents` and link bill→journal (`posts`) and payment→bills (`pays`) so the document-flow chain spans the AP flow. Migration `0012_finance_ap` creates four tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); autogenerate confirms zero model drift on SQLite.
- **D-032 Background-job core (PLAN 4P.5, closes #26): code-defined registry + in-process asyncio runner behind a scheduler seam; `core_jobs` not audited:** `core/jobs.py` owns the `Job` model (`core_jobs`: job_type/status/payload/result/error/submitted_by/started+finished, indexes `(tenant_id, status)` + `(tenant_id, job_type, created_at)`; migration 0017), a `@register_job` registry (code-defined like permissions), `submit_job` (PENDING row flushed inside the endpoint's uow so it commits atomically with the D-013 idempotency capture — a replayed key returns the SAME job id), and the runner: scheduled via `schedule_job(job_id, session_factory)` strictly AFTER the uow commit (no visibility race), it opens its own session from the factory the router's `get_session_factory` dependency supplied (production = app factory; tests = the per-test-engine override, which is how the runner lands in the right DB in both worlds), restores `tenant_context(tenant_id)` + the D-010 actor ContextVar from `submitted_by_user_id`, marks RUNNING (own commit), runs the handler inside `run_in_uow` with COMPLETED+result set in the same uow (business writes and terminal status are atomic; events + audit behave exactly as in-request), and on any exception commits only FAILED + the truncated error. Concurrency capped at 4 via per-event-loop semaphores (asyncio primitives bind to their first loop; tests run one loop per test); `wait_for_jobs()` makes tests deterministic. SWAP SEAM: submitters call `schedule_job`, delegating to the module `scheduler: JobScheduler` Protocol singleton (the D-011 bus pattern) — a queue runner (arq/celery) rebinds it, ignoring the session-factory argument, with zero submitter changes. Polling: `core/jobs_router.py` (`GET /api/v1/jobs[/{id}]`, auth-only + tenant-scoped, paginated — the D-027 core-router precedent). `core_jobs` is deliberately NOT audited: high-churn control rows (PENDING→RUNNING→terminal per job), same documented exclusion class as `core_refresh_sessions`/`core_idempotency_keys`; the handler's BUS

Service split: `service/customer_invoices.py` (draft+post), `service/customer_receipts.py` (receipt document + clearing), `service/ar_aging.py` (projection), `service/dunning.py`. **Generalized AP's clearing into a shared helper:** AP's `service/payment_clearing.py` was NOT reusable as-is (it took `VendorBill` objects + AP error codes), but the realized-FX MATH is identical at the customer side — so the engine-agnostic core (compute functional amounts, build the balanced clearing journal lines with explicit functional amounts via `skip_translation`, the realized-FX gain/loss line) was factored into a NEW `service/clearing_fx.py` keyed on plain `ClearedItem` tuples + a `control_is_debit` flag (AP debits the control to clear, AR credits it — the gain/loss direction inverts: AP realized = func_control − func_bank, AR realized = func_bank − func_control). `payment_clearing.py` was refactored to adapt bills into `ClearedItem`s and delegate; AR's receipts do the same with invoices — ONE FX implementation, no duplication. **Dunning** (the AR-only escalation, no AP mirror): `DUNNING_THRESHOLDS = (7, 30, 60)` days map to levels 1/2/3 via `dunning_level_for(days_overdue)`; `run_dunning(as_of)` scans OPEN overdue invoices, and when the level their age earns EXCEEDS the invoice's current `dunning_level` it raises it + stamps `last_dunned_date = as_of`, returning the notice list — it posts NO journal (dunning is state only, D-029) and is idempotent-ish per day (a re-run advances nothing already at its earned level). Permissions `finance.ar.read`/`.manage`/`.collect` (collect = receipts + dunning). `queries.py` adds `get_open_customer_invoices` + `customer_open_balance` (the latter for Sales' future credit-limit block, partner-keyed by the opaque `partner_id`). Migration `0013_finance_ar` creates four tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); autogenerate confirms zero drift on SQLite AND Postgres. **Deviation (PG identifier cap):** the D-022 auto FK names for the two `fin_customer_receipt_allocations` composite FKs would be 67 chars (> PG's 63), so the model + migration share explicit abbreviated names (`fk_fin_cust_receipt_allocs_tenant_id_{receipts,invoices}`) — same precedent as AP's abbreviated allocation UNIQUE name (D-030). Finance stays the bottom dependency (imports no module above it; verified); `partner_id` stays opaque (plain Uuid, no FK).
- **D-030 AP (PLAN 4.5) placement + the journal `skip_translation` clearing hook (implements D-029/D-019):** the four AP tables live in `finance/models/payables.py` (re-exported from `models/__init__`); AP request/response schemas live in a NEW sibling `finance/payables_schemas.py` and the AP endpoints in a NEW sibling `finance/ap_router.py` — both siblings (not a `schemas/`/`router/` package) exactly mirror the sanctioned `fx_router.py`/`tax_router.py` precedent, because `schemas.py`/`router.py` are at the STRUCTURE §3 400-line cap and the AP surface is self-contained; `ap_router` mounts into the finance router via the same `include_router` one-surface pattern (no second mount in main.py). The AP service is split across `service/vendor_bills.py` (draft + post), `service/payment_clearing.py` (open-item validation + realized-FX line construction), `service/vendor_payments.py` (payment document + run), and `service/ap_aging.py` (the projection) to keep every file under the cap. **Realized FX at clearing (D-019):** computed per cleared bill as `functional-at-bill-rate − functional-at-payment-rate` over the cleared transaction amount (the bill's frozen rate is read from its posted AP-control journal line, not re-looked-up), posted to the `fx_realized_gain`/`fx_realized_loss` posting-default account inside the SAME payment entry. This required a behaviour-preserving extension to `service/journal.post_entry`: a new keyword `skip_translation: bool = False` — when the caller has already set explicit per-line functional amounts (the only case where functional ≠ transaction × a single entry rate), the engine validates those balance instead of re-translating. The realized-FX line is denominated in the functional currency and carries a positive transaction amount equal to its functional amount, so the per-line one-side CHECK (D-017, on transaction amounts) holds while the balance trigger (functional sums only) balances — no zero/zero line. Open items are partner-keyed by the opaque `partner_id` stamped on the AP control line (D-029); finance imports no module above it (verified). AP documents register in `core_documents` and link bill→journal (`posts`) and payment→bills (`pays`) so the document-flow chain spans the AP flow. Migration `0012_finance_ap` creates four tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); autogenerate confirms zero model drift on SQLite.
- **D-032 Background-job core (PLAN 4P.5, closes #26): code-defined registry + in-process asyncio runner behind a scheduler seam; `core_jobs` not audited:** `core/jobs.py` owns the `Job` model (`core_jobs`: job_type/status/payload/result/error/submitted_by/started+finished, indexes `(tenant_id, status)` + `(tenant_id, job_type, created_at)`; migration 0017), a `@register_job` registry (code-defined like permissions), `submit_job` (PENDING row flushed inside the endpoint's uow so it commits atomically with the D-013 idempotency capture — a replayed key returns the SAME job id), and the runner: scheduled via `schedule_job(job_id, session_factory)` strictly AFTER the uow commit (no visibility race), it opens its own session from the factory the router's `get_session_factory` dependency supplied (production = app factory; tests = the per-test-engine override, which is how the runner lands in the right DB in both worlds), restores `tenant_context(tenant_id)` + the D-010 actor ContextVar from `submitted_by_user_id`, marks RUNNING (own commit), runs the handler inside `run_in_uow` with COMPLETED+result set in the same uow (business writes and terminal status are atomic; events + audit behave exactly as in-request), and on any exception commits only FAILED + the truncated error. Concurrency capped at 4 via per-event-loop semaphores (asyncio primitives bind to their first loop; tests run one loop per test); `wait_for_jobs()` makes tests deterministic. SWAP SEAM: submitters call `schedule_job`, delegating to the module `scheduler: JobScheduler` Protocol singleton (the D-011 bus pattern) — a queue runner (arq/celery) rebinds it, ignoring the session-factory argument, with zero submitter changes. Polling: `core/jobs_router.py` (`GET /api/v1/jobs[/{id}]`, auth-only + tenant-scoped, paginated — the D-027 core-router precedent). `core_jobs` is deliberately NOT audited: high-churn control rows (PENDING→RUNNING→terminal per job), same documented exclusion class as `core_refresh_sessions`/`core_idempotency_keys`; the handler's BUSINESS writes are audited normally with the submitting user as actor. The #26 fix: `POST /finance/fx-revaluation-runs` and `POST /finance/payment-runs` now submit `finance.fx_revaluation`/`finance.payment_run` jobs and return `202 {job_id, status}` (service functions unchanged; the retired sync `PaymentRunResult` wrapper was deleted — payment ids/numbers ride the job result). Model registration deviation: `core/jobs` imports `core/audit` (actor ContextVar), so like idempotency it registers on `Base.metadata` from the BOTTOM of `core/db.py`, not models.py's trailing imports (a trailing import dead-locks on the audit->models cycle).
- **D-033 Bank reconciliation (PLAN 4.9) placement + statement-as-external-document + match-rule boundary:** the two bank tables live in `finance/models/bank.py`; the service splits along concerns (`service/bank_csv.py` CSV contract, `service/bank_import.py` import/job/progress, `service/bank_reconcile.py` matching/clearing) and the HTTP surface is the sanctioned sibling pair `bank_schemas.py`/`bank_router.py` (D-030 precedent), all under the STRUCTURE cap. `BankStatement` gets DocumentMixin (the task sketch omitted it) because the required docflow statement->'posts'->clearing-entry link (D-012) needs a registry row — but NO gapless number is claimed: D-012 numbering covers documents Atlas issues, and a statement is an EXTERNAL document identified by bank account + date + source_filename, so its registry doc_number stays NULL. `matched_journal_line_id` is an opaque Uuid (read-only reference into the immutable journal, the dimension-id precedent); `cleared_journal_entry_id` is a composite tenant FK (the entry is created BY this flow). `import_job_id` is a plain nullable Uuid (the core_jobs attribution precedent), stamped via the router writing the job id back into the job payload after submit_job (a handler cannot know its own job id). Bulk insert uses the ORM-enabled `insert(Model)` executemany with explicit per-row tenant_id — sanctioned: it is an ORM statement (not a Core Table insert), inserts are not tenant-filtered by D-007 (values carry tenant_id; composite FKs backstop), and the grep gate bans only attribute-call inserts/raw SQL. Match rules v1 = exact amount+date, then exact amount ±3 days (nearest-wins, single consumption tenant-wide); the rule-3 doc-number-in-description heuristic, partial/many-to-one matching and tolerance bands are documented boundary (parity doc already lists MT940/CAMT + auto-clearing rules as laters). Statement lists sort (statement_date DESC, id) WITHOUT a created_at seek key: SQLite stores server-default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP without fractional seconds while a re-bound cursor datetime renders with `.000000`, so a created_at key lexicographically re-includes the boundary row — a pre-existing core/pagination.py issue affecting every created_at-sorted list on SQLite (PG unaffected), tracked for a core-level fix.
- **D-034 Asset accounting lite (PLAN 4.10) placement + the depreciation-run shape + the finance constants package split:** the three tables live in `finance/models/assets.py`; the service splits along concerns (`service/assets.py` register lifecycle, `service/depreciation.py` formula + posting run + job handler, `service/depreciation_read.py` reads + the register projection — the journal.py/journal_read.py cap-split precedent) and the HTTP surface is the sanctioned sibling pair `assets_schemas.py`/`assets_router.py` (D-030 precedent), mounted one-surface. **Idempotency backbone:** `UNIQUE(tenant_id, asset_id, fiscal_period_id)` on `fin_depreciation_entries` — an asset depreciates once per period EVER, so overlapping/concurrent runs collide at the DB; the run engine selects eligible assets with a NOT EXISTS anti-join, reads prior accumulated+count in ONE grouped aggregate, bulk-inserts entries with ONE executemany, and posts ONE journal entry with lines GROUPED per (expense account, cost centre)/per accumulated account (PERFORMANCE §2: the SQL statement count is constant in the asset count, query-counter pinned). A re-run for a finished period returns the existing POSTED run unchanged (the allocation idempotency pattern); the endpoint is additionally D-013 Idempotent and routes >100 eligible assets to a `finance.depreciation_run` job (202, the bank-import threshold pattern). **Exactness:** STRAIGHT_LINE uses the drift-free cumulative formulation (amount(n) = quantize(depreciable×n/life) − prior_accumulated; final period absorbs the residual) so schedules sum to cost−salvage EXACTLY; DECLINING_BALANCE floors at salvage (the crossing/exhaust period takes NBV−salvage, landing exactly on salvage). `compute_depreciation` takes a 1-based schedule `period_index` (prior entry count + 1) rather than a period object — the formula depends on schedule position, not calendar identity. NO stored NBV: the register endpoint recomputes accumulated/NBV from SUM over entries bounded by periods ending ≤ as_of (D-021 spirit); the entries' `*_after` columns are per-entry audit trail only. AssetStatus is DRAFT|ACTIVE|FULLY_DEPRECIATED only — DISPOSED is NOT in the enum (no dead values; disposal/transfer/parallel areas are recorded parity laters). The AST number is claimed at ACTIVATION (the asset's claim-at-permanence moment, D-012; partial-unique backstop), the DEP number at run posting. Three composite FKs from fin_assets to fin_accounts carry explicit abbreviated names (the D-022 column-0 convention would collide three ways). Migration `0019_finance_assets` creates three tables and alters nothing (no trigger-bearing table touched, D-022); zero autogen drift on both engines. **Constants package split (STRUCTURE §8.4):** `finance/constants.py` hit the 400-line hard cap when 4.10's enums/sequences/permissions landed, so it split into the `finance/constants/` package (`enums.py`, `documents.py`, `permissions.py`) with `__init__.py` re-exporting every name — the same §3 package rule models/ and service/ used; zero import-site changes. Test-side: `_FINANCE_KEYS` in tests factories is now derived from `core.rbac.catalog_keys()` (every registered `finance.*` key), self-extending like the tenancy mapper enumeration; the 4.10 builders live in `tests/modules/finance/factories_assets.py` because factories.py is at the cap.
- **D-035 Conditional requests on slow-changing reference data (PLAN 4P.6, closes #28): collection-level WEAK ETag in a new `core/conditional.py`:** a justified core flat file (the `core/pagination.py` precedent) holds `collection_etag` (ONE cheap aggregate `SELECT COUNT(id), MAX(updated_at)` over the model — auto tenant-scoped by the D-007 `do_orm_execute` listener because the `func` aggregate references the model's mapped columns, verified), `check_not_modified` (RFC 7232 weak comparison, handles the `W/` prefix and `*`), and `conditional_response` (the 304-or-200 epilogue: on an `If-None-Match` hit it returns a bare starlette `Response(304, {ETag})` WITHOUT awaiting the page builder — so FastAPI's `response_model=Page[T]` is bypassed and the page query never runs, making the 304 path cheaper than 200: 2 queries vs 3, query-counter pinned). Format `W/"<count>-<max_updated_micros>-<tenant8>-<request_fingerprint>"`. **Collection-level, not row-level**, because a list endpoint returns a page of a collection and `(count, max_updated)` is the cheapest sound "did anything change?" validator — any insert moves count, any update moves `MAX(updated_at)` (TimestampMixin.onupdate), any delete moves count; trade-off is that any change invalidates every page's validator, accepted for the small reference sets this covers. **The `tenant8` component** makes a cross-tenant 304 impossible even though the aggregate is already tenant-filtered. **The `request_fingerprint`** (cursor+limit+filters, reusing `pagination.filter_fingerprint`) is the key correctness point: it is folded into the ETag so a 304 can only ever be served for the IDENTICAL page request and never returns the wrong slice. Applied to the seven slow-changing reference lists ONLY (`accounts`, `account-groups`, `currencies`, `tax-codes`, `fiscal-years`, `fiscal-periods`, `posting-defaults`); transactional lists (journal-entries, bills, invoices, receipts, payments, exchange-rates, bank-statements, depreciation/reval runs, jobs) deliberately carry none. **Structure deviation:** adding `request`/`response` + the etag computation pushed `finance/router.py` over the 400-line cap, so the journal-entry endpoints moved to a new sanctioned sibling `finance/journal_router.py` (the `fx_router.py`/`tax_router.py` one-surface precedent) — a behaviour-preserving extraction, journal is a distinct aggregate from the COA/fiscal reference data; router.py is now 322 lines.
- **D-036 Inventory stock model (PLAN 5.2): the move ledger is the quantity SSOT, the quant is a maintained projection, negative stock is forbidden at service + CHECK on both engines:** `inv_stock_moves` is an **append-only, POSTED-at-creation, immutable** ledger (no draft phase — unlike journals which are DRAFT→POSTED — because a move IS the ledger; corrections are reversing moves, never edits, the D-017 reversal philosophy applied to stock). `quantity` is **always positive**; `move_type` (RECEIPT/ISSUE/TRANSFER/ADJUSTMENT) decides which of from_bin/to_bin participate via the greppable `constants.MOVE_BIN_SIDES` table (RECEIPT→to only, ISSUE→from only, TRANSFER→both-distinct, ADJUSTMENT→exactly-one-side), so direction is structural not a sign — the journal one-sided-amount philosop

1	# GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md — Repository & GitHub Operating Protocol for Atlas ERP
2	
3	Place this file at the repo root alongside CLAUDE.md, and add this line to CLAUDE.md: "All git and GitHub operations MUST follow GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md. Re-read it after any compaction." You (the agent) use the `gh` CLI for everything GitHub-side: repo creation, PRs, issues, labels, releases.
4	
5	# 1. Repository Setup (do this once, before any code)
6	
7	1. Create a **public** repository: `gh repo create atlas-erp --public --description "Open-source, industry-agnostic ERP. Functional benchmark: SAP S/4HANA." --clone`. Because the repo is public from day one: never commit secrets, tokens, API keys, real personal data, or `.env` files — commit `.env.example` instead, and add a `.gitignore` covering env files, virtualenvs, node_modules, build output, and IDE folders as your very first commit.
8	2. Add at the root: `README.md`, `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0), `CONTRIBUTING.md` (summarizes this workflow for human contributors), `SECURITY.md` (how to report vulnerabilities privately), and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` plus `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yaml` and `feature.yaml` matching the formats defined below.
9	3. Create labels: `bug`, `enhancement`, `tech-debt`, `module:finance`, `module:inventory`, `module:procurement`, `module:sales`, `module:manufacturing`, `module:hr`, `module:core`, `module:frontend`, `module:docs`, `severity:blocker`, `severity:major`, `severity:minor`, `found-during-build`.
10	4. Create a CI workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs on every PR: backend lint (ruff) + pytest, frontend typecheck + build. A red CI run blocks merging — no exceptions, including for you.
11	
12	# 2. Branch Model — exactly two long-lived branches
13	
14	- **`main` = production.** Always releasable. Nothing is ever committed directly to `main`. It only ever receives merges from `dev` via a promotion PR (section 5).
15	- **`dev` = integration.** All work lands here first, via short-lived feature branches.
16	- **Feature branches** are cut from `dev`, named `feat/<module>-<short-slug>`, `fix/<issue-number>-<short-slug>`, or `docs/<short-slug>`. One branch = one task from PLAN.md or one issue. Delete the branch after its PR merges. Never let a feature branch live longer than one task — long-lived feature branches are how you lose state across compactions.
17	- Set `main` as the default branch on GitHub, and enable branch protection on both `main` and `dev` requiring CI to pass before merge (`gh api` or repo settings).
18	
19	# 3. Commit Discipline
20	
21	- Use Conventional Commits: `feat(finance): reject journal entries with unbalanced lines`, `fix(inventory): correct FIFO layer consumption on partial issue (#23)`, `test(sales): add credit-limit block coverage`, `docs(readme): add ERD`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `test`, `docs`, `refactor`, `chore`, `ci`.
22	- One logical change per commit. A commit must leave the codebase in a working state — tests passing — because commits are also your recovery checkpoints after compaction.
23	- Commit body (the detail level): 2–6 lines explaining **why**, not what (the diff shows what). State the business rule or invariant involved, any alternative you rejected, and reference the PLAN.md task number and any issue (`Refs PLAN 4.3`, `Fixes #23`). A future maintainer reading only `git log` should be able to reconstruct the reasoning of the build.
24	- Never use `--force` on `dev` or `main`. Never amend or rebase commits that have been pushed to a shared branch.
25	
26	# 4. Pull Requests into `dev`
27	
28	Every task merges to `dev` through a PR — even though you are the only contributor — because PRs are the project's reviewable history and your own audit trail. Open with `gh pr create --base dev`.
29	
30	**PR title:** same convention as commits, scoped to the task: `feat(finance): double-entry journal engine with period close`.
31	
32	**PR description — required sections, this is the expected level of detail:**
33	1. **Summary** — 2–4 sentences: what this delivers in business terms ("Posting a goods receipt now creates an inventory-debit / GR-IR-credit journal automatically").
34	2. **Design notes** — the decisions made and why, mirroring what was added to DECISIONS.md. Include rejected alternatives if any were seriously considered.
35	3. **Invariants enforced** — list any business rules this PR adds or relies on (e.g., "debits must equal credits per currency, enforced in service layer + DB CHECK").
36	4. **Tests** — what is covered, what intentionally isn't yet, with the issue number for the gap.
37	5. **Linked items** — `Refs PLAN x.y`, `Closes #NN` for every issue resolved.
38	6. **Out of scope** — anything noticed but deliberately not done here (each must have an issue, see section 6).
39	
40	Apply the relevant `module:*` label. Before merging: confirm CI is green, re-read your own diff once (`gh pr diff`) looking specifically for secrets, debug prints, and tenant-filter bypasses, then merge with **squash** (`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`) so `dev` history stays one-commit-per-task. The squash commit message must keep the PR title and a condensed body.
41	
42	# 5. Promotion: `dev` → `main`
43	
44	Promote when a milestone is complete and stable — at minimum after each major phase of PLAN.md (core complete, finance complete, all backend modules complete, frontend complete, v1 final). Never promote mid-task.
45	
46	Promotion procedure:
47	1. On `dev`: full test suite green, `docker-compose up` verified working, PROGRESS.md and the parity doc updated.
48	2. Open a **promotion PR** `dev → main` titled `release: <milestone name>` (`gh pr create --base main --head dev`). Its description is a **changelog**: every squashed PR since the last promotion grouped under Added / Fixed / Changed, the list of issues closed, known issues still open (with numbers), and any migration or breaking-change notes. This description is the release notes — write it for an outside user of the public repo, not for yourself.
49	3. Merge with a **merge commit** (`gh pr merge --merge`), NOT squash — `main`'s history should show promotions as merge points while preserving traceability to dev.
50	4. Tag the merge commit semver: `v0.1.0` (core), `v0.2.0` (finance), … `v1.0.0` (final), and create a GitHub release: `gh release create v0.x.0 --notes-from-tag` or paste the changelog. 
51	5. Never cherry-pick individual commits to `main`. If production needs an urgent fix, branch `fix/...` from `main`, PR it back to `main`, then immediately merge `main` back into `dev` so the branches never diverge.
52	
53	# 6. Issue-First Bug & Debt Handling (mandatory)
54	
55	When you discover ANY problem mid-build — a bug, a design flaw, missing validation, a test gap, tech debt — you do not silently fix it. The protocol is **file first, fix second**:
56	
57	1. **File the issue immediately** with `gh issue create`, labels `found-during-build` + `bug`/`tech-debt` + `module:*` + `severity:*`. Required body:
58	   - **What's wrong** — observed behavior vs. expected, with the exact file/function.
59	   - **Reproduction** — the failing input, test, or scenario.
60	   - **Impact** — which invariant or feature it threatens (e.g., "allows posting to a closed period via the API but not the UI — financial-integrity blocker").
61	   - **Proposed fix** — your initial plan, 1–3 lines.
62	2. **Triage by severity:** `severity:blocker` (breaks a financial/stock invariant, tenant isolation, or auth) — stop current work and fix it now. `severity:major` — fix before the current module's PR merges. `severity:minor` — leave it open, schedule it before the next promotion to `main`. Update PLAN.md with a task entry for every non-blocker issue so it can't be forgotten after compaction.
63	3. **Fix on a branch** named `fix/<issue-number>-<slug>`. The fix PR must: reference `Closes #NN`, include a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it (no fix merges without one), and explain root cause in the Design notes — not just the symptom.
64	4. **Close via merge**, never manually, so the issue links to the fixing PR. If investigation shows the issue was invalid, close it with a comment explaining why — never close silently.
65	5. An issue may NOT be open and untracked at promotion time: every open issue at a `dev → main` promotion must appear in the promotion PR's "known issues" section.
66	
67	# 7. Documentation Handling
68	
69	- Docs live in the repo, versioned with the code: `README.md` (front door: what Atlas is, the S/4HANA benchmark framing, screenshots, <10-step quickstart, architecture + ERD Mermaid diagrams), `docs/` (architecture.md, module guides — one per module, written as you finish each module, not at the end —, api.md pointing at the OpenAPI spec, industry-templates.md, and `docs/research/s4hana-parity.md`), plus CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md.
70	- **Docs are part of the task**: a module's PR is not complete without its module guide updated. `docs(...)`-only changes still go through feature branch → PR → `dev`.
71	- The internal state files (PLAN.md, PROGRESS.md, DECISIONS.md, CLAUDE.md, this file) are committed too — in a public repo they double as a transparent build journal. Keep their tone professional; they will be read by strangers.
72	- README badges: CI status, license, latest release. Update the README's feature list at every promotion so `main`'s README never advertises something `main` doesn't contain.
73	
74	# 8. Public-Repo Hygiene (continuous)
75	
76	- Before EVERY push: scan the diff for secrets, internal URLs, personal data, and seed data containing realistic-looking real names/emails (use clearly fictional seed identities and `example.com` emails).
77	- If a secret ever lands in history: rotate it immediately, then file a `severity:blocker` issue documenting the exposure and remediation.
78	- All third-party code/licenses must be compatible with Apache-2.0; note any attributions in a `NOTICE` file.
79	
80	# 9. Self-Check Loop
81	
82	At the end of every work session (and after any compaction recovery), run this checklist and append the result to PROGRESS.md: working tree clean? current branch correct? all merged branches deleted? CI green on `dev`? any discovered-but-unfiled problems? any open `severity:blocker`? docs current for everything merged? If any answer is bad, fixing it is the next task.

- **`main` = production.** Always releasable. Nothing is ever committed directly to `main`. It only ever receives merges from `dev` via a promotion PR (section 5).
- **`dev` = integration.** All work lands here first, via short-lived feature branches.
- **Feature branches** are cut from `dev`, named `feat/<module>-<short-slug>`, `fix/<issue-number>-<short-slug>`, or `docs/<short-slug>`. One branch = one task from PLAN.md or one issue. Delete the branch after its PR merges. Never let a feature branch live longer than one task — long-lived feature branches are how you lose state across compactions.
- Set `main` as the default branch on GitHub, and enable branch protection on both `main` and `dev` requiring CI to pass before merge (`gh api` or repo settings).

# 3. Commit Discipline

- Use Conventional Commits: `feat(finance): reject journal entries with unbalanced lines`, `fix(inventory): correct FIFO layer consumption on partial issue (#23)`, `test(sales): add credit-limit block coverage`, `docs(readme): add ERD`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `test`, `docs`, `refactor`, `chore`, `ci`.
- One logical change per commit. A commit must leave the codebase in a working state — tests passing — because commits are also your recovery checkpoints after compaction.
- Commit body (the detail level): 2–6 lines explaining **why**, not what (the diff shows what). State the business rule or invariant involved, any alternative you rejected, and reference the PLAN.md task number and any issue (`Refs PLAN 4.3`, `Fixes #23`). A future maintainer reading only `git log` should be able to reconstruct the reasoning of the build.
- Never use `--force` on `dev` or `main`. Never amend or rebase commits that have been pushed to a shared branch.

# 4. Pull Requests into `dev`

Every task merges to `dev` through a PR — even though you are the only contributor — because PRs are the project's reviewable history and your own audit trail. Open with `gh pr create --base dev`.

**PR title:** same convention as commits, scoped to the task: `feat(finance): double-entry journal engine with period close`.

**PR description — required sections, this is the expected level of detail:**
1. **Summary** — 2–4 sentences: what this delivers in business terms ("Posting a goods receipt now creates an inventory-debit / GR-IR-credit journal automatically").
2. **Design notes** — the decisions made and why, mirroring what was added to DECISIONS.md. Include rejected alternatives if any were seriously considered.
3. **Invariants enforced** — list any business rules this PR adds or relies on (e.g., "debits must equal credits per currency, enforced in service layer + DB CHECK").
4. **Tests** — what is covered, what intentionally isn't yet, with the issue number for the gap.
5. **Linked items** — `Refs PLAN x.y`, `Closes #NN` for every issue resolved.
6. **Out of scope** — anything noticed but deliberately not done here (each must have an issue, see section 6).

Apply the relevant `module:*` label. Before merging: confirm CI is green, re-read your own diff once (`gh pr diff`) looking specifically for secrets, debug prints, and tenant-filter bypasses, then merge with **squash** (`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`) so `dev` history stays one-commit-per-task. The squash commit message must keep the PR title and a condensed body.

# 5. Promotion: `dev` → `main`

Promote when a milestone is complete and stable — at minimum after each major phase of PLAN.md (core complete, finance complete, all backend modules complete, frontend complete, v1 final). Never promote mid-task.

Promotion procedure:
1. On `dev`: full test suite green, `docker-compose up` verified working, PROGRESS.md and the parity doc updated.
2. Open a **promotion PR** `dev → main` titled `release: <milestone name>` (`gh pr create --base main --head dev`). Its description is a **changelog**: every squashed PR since the last promotion grouped under Added / Fixed / Changed, the list of issues closed, known issues still open (with numbers), and any migration or breaking-change notes. This description is the release notes — write it for an outside user of the public repo, not for yourself.
3. Merge with a **merge commit** (`gh pr merge --merge`), NOT squash — `main`'s history should show promotions as merge points while preserving traceability to dev.
4. Tag the merge commit semver: `v0.1.0` (core), `v0.2.0` (finance), … `v1.0.0` (final), and create a GitHub release: `gh release create v0.x.0 --notes-from-tag` or paste the changelog. 
5. Never cherry-pick individual commits to `main`. If production needs an urgent fix, branch `fix/...` from `main`, PR it back to `main`, then immediately merge `main` back into `dev` so the branches never diverge.

# 6. Issue-First Bug & Debt Handling (mandatory)

When you discover ANY problem mid-build — a bug, a design flaw, missing validation, a test gap, tech debt — you do not silently fix it. The protocol is **file first, fix second**:

1. **File the issue immediately** with `gh issue create`, labels `found-during-build` + `bug`/`tech-debt` + `module:*` + `severity:*`. Required body:
   - **What's wrong** — observed behavior vs. expected, with the exact file/function.
   - **Reproduction** — the failing input, test, or scenario.
   - **Impact** — which invariant or feature it threatens (e.g., "allows posting to a closed period via the API but not the UI — financial-integrity blocker").
   - **Proposed fix** — your initial plan, 1–3 lines.
2. **Triage by severity:** `severity:blocker` (breaks a financial/stock invariant, tenant isolation, or auth) — stop current work and fix it now. `severity:major` — fix before the current module's PR merges. `severity:minor` — leave it open, schedule it before the next promotion to `main`. Update PLAN.md with a task entry for every non-blocker issue so it can't be forgotten after compaction.
3. **Fix on a branch** named `fix/<issue-number>-<slug>`. The fix PR must: reference `Closes #NN`, include a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it (no fix merges without one), and explain root cause in the Design notes — not just the symptom.
4. **Close via merge**, never manually, so the issue links to the fixing PR. If investigation shows the issue was invalid, close it with a comment explaining why — never close silently.
5. An issue may NOT be open and untracked at promotion time: every open issue at a `dev → main` promotion must appear in the promotion PR's "known issues" section.

# 7. Documentation Handling

- Docs live in the repo, versioned with the code: `README.md` (front door: what Atlas is, the S/4HANA benchmark framing, screenshots, <10-step quickstart, architecture + ERD Mermaid diagrams), `docs/` (architecture.md, module guides — one per module, written as you finish each module, not at the end —, api.md pointing at the OpenAPI spec, industry-templates.md, and `docs/research/s4hana-parity.md`), plus CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md.
- **Docs are part of the task**: a module's PR is not complete without its module guide updated. `docs(...)`-only changes still go through feature branch → PR → `dev`.
- The internal state files (PLAN.md, PROGRESS.md, DECISIONS.md, CLAUDE.md, this file) are committed too — in a public repo they double as a transparent build journal. Keep their tone professional; they will be read by strangers.
- README badges: CI status, license, latest release. Update the README's feature list at every promotion so `main`'s README never advertises something `main` doesn't contain.

# 8. Public-Repo Hygiene (continuous)

- Before EVERY push: scan the diff for secrets, internal URLs, personal data, and seed data containing realistic-looking real names/emails (use clearly fictional seed identities and `example.com` emails).
- If a secret ever lands in history: rotate it immediately, then file a `severity:blocker` issue documenting the exposure and remediation.
- All third-party code/licenses must be compatible with Apache-2.0; note any attributions in a `NOTICE` file.

# 9. Self-Check Loop

At the end of every work session (and after any compaction recovery), run this checklist and append the result to PROGRESS.md: working tree clean? current branch correct? all merged branches deleted? CI green on `dev`? any discovered-but-unfiled problems? any open `severity:blocker`? docs current for everything merged? If any answer is bad, fixing it is the next task.
